title: Retrospective Study to Evaluate the Typical Clinical and Radiological Parameters of Primary Bone Lymphoma
summary: Malignant lymphoma of the bone is a very rare tumour entity that affects about 5% of all patients with malignant bone tumours. In advanced stages of the disease, it is sometimes impossible to distinguish between primary lymphoma of the bone or secondary involvement. Approximately 4% of all patients with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma show an obvious osseous lesion, in bone marrow biopsies it is about 20%. In many cases of osseous lymphoma, the diagnosis is delayed due to the non-specific changes in the native X-ray image. Due to the sometimes extensive soft tissue component, Ewing's sarcoma may also be suspected in younger patients. In some cases, histological work-up is problematic and can lead to misdiagnosis of sarcoma if lymphoma is not considered. The aim is to record the symptoms, typical radiology and the course of the disease in patients with primary lymphomas of the bone.

interventions.name: All patients with bone lymphoma and surgical procedure in the study clinic.A retrospective evaluation of clinical data such as disease development, extent and therapy is perfomed. The target parameter is overall survival.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients with lymphoma of the bone who were surgically treated at our clinic during the study period.
Exclusion criteria:
None
